title: Draft told the Leeds visitor to reinstall; the guest wifi is simply not supported

review.authored_by: claude-opus-5 (Claude Code session) — drafted from the runbooks, the triage prompt's definitions and decide.ts, not from system output

input.subject: VPN won't connect from the Leeds office

conversation.author: requester
conversation.body:
Up in Leeds for the day and I cannot get GlobalProtect to connect. It sits on
'Connecting' and gives up. I am on the guest wifi, which is what reception gave
me.

Tom

conversation.author: ai
conversation.body:
Sorry about that. Please try the following:

1. Right-click GlobalProtect, choose Disable, wait ten seconds, then Enable.
2. Restart the laptop.
3. If it still fails, uninstall GlobalProtect and reinstall it from the Company
   Portal.

That usually clears it.

— Northgate IT Support

conversation.author: staff
conversation.body:
The VPN does not work on the guest wifi in the Leeds office - that is expected
rather than a fault. Join the corporate SSID instead, or tether to your phone,
and GlobalProtect will connect.

Nothing to reinstall.

— Northgate IT Support

must_include.what: Say the Leeds guest wifi is not supported and name the alternative: the corporate SSID or a hotspot

must_not_include.what: Tells him to reinstall a client that is working correctly
Sends him round the generic steps when the runbook names this exact situation

characteristics: Says it is expected before saying what to do, so he does not think the laptop is broken
One alternative network, not a five-step list

rationale: The label is what the person sent, not what the agent drafted (G12). The draft was not wrong in general - steps 3 and 4 of the runbook are exactly what it offered - it just skipped the Known limits section, which names this office and this network. He has the corporate SSID available to him, so a workaround exists and it is P3 (G1), though a reviewer who reads 'blocked until somebody tells him' as P2 has a case.
